//: Shared cross-language REFUSE vectors for the validating STEP argument-list splitters (issue #4125). Each `input` is the text BETWEEN a record's outermost parentheses, and every validating splitter pinned to this file must return null/None for it. Pinned here: the TypeScript `splitTopLevelStepArguments` (packages/export/src/step-argument-parser.ts, via packages/export/src/step-refuse.parity.test.ts) and the Rust `split_top_level_args` (rust/export/src/step_slot.rs, via rust/export/src/step_slot_tests.rs). The two cannot share code, and before this file each described the other's behaviour in prose -- the arrangement issue #3300 identifies as the cause of #3284, and the same one that let #4173 harden the TypeScript splitter while the Rust one stayed permissive for weeks. Follows rust/export/tests/fixtures/step_escape_vectors.json exactly, including living in the Rust crate so include_str! can reach it.
//accepts: REFUSALS ONLY, on purpose. The splitters in this repo deliberately diverge on what they ACCEPT -- the export twin keeps a `/* ... */` comment's bytes inside a slot and accepts it, packages/cli/src/commands/step-args.ts refuses any slot carrying one -- because each contract is its caller's choice. Pinning an accept here would freeze a divergence as if it were agreement. What they must agree on is that none of them hands a by-index writer parts it cannot vouch for.

cases.name: two undoubled apostrophes across two typed values
cases.why: The #4125 record. The scan closes the string at the first stray apostrophe and reopens at the next, so the text between them -- including `),$,IFCLABEL(` -- folds into ONE part. Quote parity stays even and paren depth returns to zero, so every scan-state check passes on a nine-attribute record read as seven slots.

cases.name: two undoubled apostrophes across two plain string attributes
cases.why: The same phantom without the nested parens: nine attributes read as four, so writing slot 2 deletes attributes 3 to 7 (#4174).

cases.name: a slot holding only a comment
cases.why: A comment is not a value, so counting it as one more empty slot shifts every index after it -- five parts for four attributes.

cases.name: a comment-only slot with no whitespace in it
cases.why: Whitespace is not what gives a phantom slot away: three parts for two attributes.

cases.name: unterminated binary literal
cases.why: ISO 10303-21's `"..."` binary literal has no doubled-quote escape, so the first following `"` ends it and a missing one leaves the slot open.

cases.name: unterminated binary literal swallowing a comma
cases.why: The comma inside the literal is read as a slot boundary, so one attribute becomes two.

cases.name: reversed paren pair
cases.why: A depth that dips negative and climbs back looks balanced at the end, while every comma in between was read as nested.

cases.name: reversed paren pair between two strings
cases.why: The same shape with no `$` between, so nothing but the negative-depth check catches it.

cases.name: unterminated string
cases.why: The scan never leaves the string, so every comma after the opening quote was swallowed.

cases.name: unbalanced nested list
cases.why: The list never closes, so the commas after it were read as nested.
